Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 2a) demonstrates marked asymmetry in pulmonary vascularity with a diminutive right hilum and oligemic right lung, which are classic signs of chronic right pulmonary artery obstruction or stenosis associated with Takayasu arteritis. This is confirmed by the CT image (Figure 2b) showing calcification and narrowing of the right pulmonary artery, indicating a longstanding process rather than an acute embolic event.
